purpose: First-quarter wave slice for the eleventh Ruleset Card — the §1.3 backup/archival card 'Restore Point' / 'The Vault' / 'Bit Rot', the first card founded on Schedule, the roster verb that stood zero-claimed until ADR-0014 #D1 blessed it (11 of the 20-type launch canon, OD-14(a)). Slice shape mirrors the ten shipped g1 siblings: a reconnaissance opening on a floor whose only motion is scheduled, the hollow-success beat as the surprise-with-composition wave (the disaster that looks like a green checkmark), a trough where the enemy is a calendar nobody checked, and a finale built on the line's authored cruelty — 'your success metric is something you can't observe' meets 'a restore that fails in public'. Deliberately RULES-FREE (no rules block): §2.24 rule-carrier values stay in the g1 slices until the batch-D rule-adapter pass reads them for cross-type tables.
determinismNote: Authored + seeded (§7.13): same seed replays identical arrival order; the sim core owns jitter streams off this seed.
rolesNote: Every entry carries `role` = its PRIMARY threat role from threats/registry-core.json `roles[0]` (§2.1 Threat Role Taxonomy, 12-role vocabulary); wave `denominations` arrays are entry-derived, and every hard wave draws exactly TWO fronts (§2.1 Two-Front Law / §2.24).

baseline._todo: §1.7: baseline continuous, diurnal, never zero. The rhythm name is authored from the card's own words (bundle tempo._todo carries the cites): 'arrive at night in a huge burst' (§1.3) × 'arriving as a nightly convoy during a visible window band' (§3.2, :12597) — the corpus's first baseline whose PEAK is the night band and whose daytime is the queue outside it. neverZero holds here in the register this line owns: the band closes at 06:00 and opens again at dusk, and in between the board is not empty — it is HOLDING (the half-open crate with the red seal, the dwell clock, the tag nobody has rewritten); the day's arrivals are verifications, audits and disputes, and between them the belt never actually stops, it only pretends. The curve catalogue owns every number, PROVISIONAL-B.

waves.title: key.wave.1
waves.note: Rule (b) honoured: first wave of any level ALWAYS <=40% of par (§1.7). Cold Start Minute governs the first 90s of sim-time: handover no threat, one FREE conversion, signature constraint asserts harmlessly with telegraph (§1.9). On this line the harmless assertion is the quarter's first nightly convoy landing clean inside a wide-open band, crates dropping with a clunk, every checkmark green, and the only anomalies are the small grey questions the vault learns to ask out loud — a speckle on tile 9 that could be anything, a delivery log the courier forgot to sign, a customer asking a question about retention that has no answer yet. The quarter opens calm because this is the calmest-looking level in the game, and the card says that IS the point: 'the threat is invisible' (§1.3).

waves.title: key.wave.2
waves.note: Rising floor beat one — the ROUTINE catastrophe, and it is a verification failing upward. Two-Front (§2.24): the hollow success (Mimic — 'your backup job has been "succeeding" for two years while writing zero bytes', §1.3 verbatim; the registry's one legitimacy-wearing entry re-framed onto this line's status lights, the checkmark 'drawn slightly hollow', §2.9) spends data-integrity in a way nothing on screen objects to, while the restore-request desk begins its climb (Swarm — the worst-day-of-their-career call and the day-400-of-365 request, 'a customer who deletes data and wants it back from day 400 of a 365-day retention', §1.3 verbatim) spending hands on questions whose only honest answer costs money. Two tenants of the same fear, two instruments, one lesson of wave two: verification is the only proof, and the window is the constraint (§1.9 teaches-line verbatim).
waves.entropyNote: entropy budget here = f(estate age x size x (1 - maintenance spend)), NOT wave number (§2.24) — on this line maintenance spend IS the scrub and the drill: 'a continuous background process that costs IOPS and reveals corruption' (§1.3 verbatim), and the card prices the unspent version twice: the six-month stop, the fourteen-month 4KB file.

waves.title: key.wave.3
waves.note: Rule (c): 30% is 50% below the preceding peak (60%) — >=45% satisfied. Dips are where the player builds (§1.7): the drill desk, the 3-2-1 meter, the tape robot and the escrow cabinet all get their window here — pun first, sorry. But on this line the quiet has a hold problem: the chain that missed Tuesday is holding Wednesday's band ('a job that runs past the window is a partial failure that compounds into tomorrow's', §3.2 verbatim; 'jobs overlap and the chain breaks', §1.3), and the empty row behind the mesh is a trust account withdrawing in silence — 'a customer whose backups silently stopped six months ago' (§1.3 verbatim). Two fronts: concurrency x reputation — held bands starve the convoy while the spiral makes the missing crates themselves the story the quarterly review starts telling.
waves.note2: the trough is also the dwell's middle frame: nothing visible happens for exactly the reason the §1.3 sentence gives — 'it is inside your retention window'.

waves.title: key.wave.4
waves.note: Compound-wave exemplar, backup variant: the window that moved lands with the dwell that ended — the DST-shifted band runs its 'successful' job straight through the business day ('saturates your storage array for four hours while customers are working', §2.9 verbatim; Debuffer debuts here, the every-4th-wave NEW ROLE beat; unseen in waves 1-3, the registry's one throttle-everyone mechanic wearing a calendar instead of a query), while the compromise that has been sitting for its 90 quiet days is now a restore request with a date on it (Bypass/Flyer — 'ransomware that encrypts the customer's data and then sits for 90 days so it is inside your retention window', §1.3 verbatim; the registry's one entry-compromise re-framed onto time, the door it walked through already inside the keep). Two fronts: data-integrity (the copy you need is the copy the attacker counted on) x concurrency (four hours of the band running in the wrong twelve). secondIncident inside the same window because on this line every failure is two failures: one that was visible and one that was checked.
waves.secondIncident: the good copy turns out to be the one the encryption predates -> 1.8x multiplier applies (stated openly in the Codex, §2.24).

waves.title: key.wave.5
waves.note: The finale is the line's inversion completed: the traffic you serve constantly was never the traffic you're graded on ('A beautiful inversion: the traffic you serve constantly is not the traffic you're graded on', §3.2 verbatim), and the grading arrives as everybody's worst day at once — the surge pulls OUTBOUND at full tank (Tank — 'fifty customers all restore at once, and your restore capacity was sized for two', §9716 verbatim; the registry's one raw-volume entry re-worn to run the other direction, this flood is their own data coming home), while the desk drowns in exactly the calls the drills were insurance against (Swarm — the hydra of 4am phones and hourglass reads, hands spent on 'whether Tuesday's file comes back', §1.9's own customerWants line). Hard wave draws TWO fronts — bandwidth x hands — per §2.24: the pipe and the person. Win check: the band held, the checkmarks were solid, the tag got rewritten, and the one restore that mattered was fast enough to be boring.
waves.triageWindow: after any catastrophic failure in this wave: arrivals queue visibly outside, patience draining, hands freed 30s (§1.7).
